questions.q: What format does Spark expect by default when reading a JSON file?
options: Line-delimited JSON — one JSON object per line
A single giant JSON array wrapping every record
XML wrapped in JSON tags
Only CSV files renamed with a .json extension
questions.explain: Spark can read a multi-line array with multiLine=True, but the line-delimited default is what enables distributing the file across workers.

questions.q: Why does line-delimited JSON matter for Spark specifically?
options: Spark distributes a file across workers by splitting it into chunks, and one object per line lets each worker parse its chunk independently
It has no real technical reason, it's just a style preference
JSON arrays are not valid syntax in any context
Line-delimited files are always smaller in size
questions.explain: A single giant array can't be split across workers the same way, since no individual line is a complete, parseable record on its own.

questions.q: What happens to a nested JSON object, like {"pickup": {"lat": 40.7, "lon": -73.9}}, when read into a Spark DataFrame?
options: It becomes a nested struct column, accessed with dot notation like pickup.lat
Spark throws an error and refuses to read nested objects
It gets silently flattened into two separate top-level columns automatically
It's converted into a string of raw JSON text
questions.explain: Dot notation reaches into the struct the same way you'd index into a nested Python dictionary.

questions.q: How does spark.read.json() compare in shape to spark.read.csv() from Lesson 40?
options: Nearly identical — same spark.read pattern, just a different reader method for a different format
Completely different, with no shared syntax at all
JSON requires an entirely separate SparkSession
CSV files must be converted to JSON first before reading
questions.explain: This is the consistent pattern across spark.read: csv, json, and parquet all share the same basic shape.

questions.q: Can Spark read a JSON file formatted as one big array instead of line-delimited?
options: Yes, using multiLine=True, but at the cost of the distribution benefit line-delimited format provides
No, Spark can never read a JSON array under any circumstances
Only if the array has fewer than 100 records
Only after manually converting it to CSV first
questions.explain: multiLine=True works, but it gives up the per-line splitting that makes line-delimited JSON efficient to distribute.
